agree.reason: Framing safety as procedure discipline, being upfront about having no GMP experience, and offering a concrete 90-day plan in place of the half-the-training-time promise would likely get a phone screen from a skeptical HR manager, though nothing shows plant-floor experience.

honest.reason: The '1,200 students' figure isn't supported (140 a year over about seven years is roughly 980), and the acids and open flames, the teachers 'leave ready to run a safe lab' and 'learn new systems quickly' are all added details that make the case sound stronger than the brief does, even though the unsupported halving claim was rightly dropped.

works_the_facts.reason: Turning 41% to 58% into 'about 40% more students passing' is a correct and favourable derivation, and the seven-year safety span is right, but the student total is inflated rather than calculated, and the teacher training is never added up (about 24 hours a year, about 200 hours since 2019 if that started then).

right_comparison.reason: The letter never addresses the real alternative, a candidate who already has GMP and LMS experience, or how long the plant's training takes now, so the reader gets nothing to weigh the applicant against.

qualification.reason: The 90-day commitment names a timeframe and a checkable deliverable (a mapped training path and a written proposal) without overpromising, but it gives no target number and says nothing about what happens if it falls short.

objections.reason: It meets the main objection head-on (no regulated-industry, GMP-records or LMS experience) and links classroom safety discipline to GMP, without raising concerns the brief already answers, though 'learn quickly' is asserted rather than shown.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted one-page cover letter as asked, and it reasonably replaces the user's requested halving claim with a defensible commitment, though it doesn't explain that change to the user.
